items.caption: This module turns Symcon into a Modbus TCP server (slave): external Modbus clients (masters) read and write Symcon variables through the register table defined below. Both terms mean the same thing - the Modbus specification says client/server, older data sheets and devices often still say master/slave. The TCP port is set on the parent Server Socket instance (usually 502). Several simultaneous connections on the same port are possible.

Register table: Each row maps one value. 'Address' is the 0-based protocol address of the first word; multi-word types (int32/uint32/float32 = 2 words, float64 = 4 words) occupy the following addresses. 'Factor' scales from the variable to the register (register value = variable value x factor; the reverse when writing). If no variable is assigned and 'Write' is set to 'No', the 'Fixed value' is returned. If no variable is assigned but writing is allowed, the row works as a memory cell (see below).

Write (column 'Write'): 'No' = the master may only read (write attempts are acknowledged but discarded). 'Yes - action' = a value written by the master is passed to the variable via RequestAction if it has an action (e.g. a write access switches an actuator), otherwise via SetValue. 'Yes - direct' = always SetValue, the variable's action is deliberately NOT triggered - required when the variable belongs to another instance (e.g. a register of a ModBus device) whose action would otherwise try to write the value to a completely different device.

Memory cell (row without a variable, Write set to 'Yes'): As with a classic Modbus server (e.g. ModRSsim2), the register remembers the value written by the master and returns it on the next read - permanently, even after a restart. The 'Fixed value' is only the start value until the first write access. The write variants 'action' and 'direct' behave the same here. Typical use: setpoint registers that a direct marketer writes and a ModBus device (or another device on your own network) reads back from this server. The value is shown in the 'Value' column; if the row is deleted or assigned to a variable, the remembered value is discarded. The timeout protection also works with memory cells (the fallback value is written into the cell).

Replacing an existing Modbus server (slave) (e.g. a simulator such as ModRSsim2, or a PLC): 1) Create the register table exactly like the old server - take over addresses, data types, word order and unit ID; if in doubt, leave 'Reject requests to other unit IDs' OFF at first. 2) Link the same Symcon variables as before so existing scripts/events keep working unchanged; if the variables belong to another instance (typically a previous ModBus device that served the old server), choose write mode 'Yes - direct'. If the previous variable is write-protected or belongs to a ModBus device that itself polls the server (setpoints that a direct marketer writes and a ModBus device reads back), leave the variable empty instead: the row becomes a memory cell, and the ModBus device reads the value from this server. 3) Stop the old server on this port, then open this instance's Server Socket on the same port. 4) Check via the connection line above ('last ... o'clock' must keep advancing at the client's polling interval) and in the instance's debug window. You can go back at any time: close the Server Socket, start the old server.

Unmapped registers: If a master requests an address for which no table row exists, the module returns either the value 0 (tolerant, default - useful when masters read whole blocks) or a Modbus exception 'Illegal Data Address' (strict - errors become visible immediately), depending on the setting.

Word order: Modbus transmits each 16-bit register big-endian. For multi-word values, the 'Low word first' option determines the word order (on = CDAB, e.g. Meteocontrol; off = ABCD, e.g. SunSpec). What the remote side expects is stated in its register documentation.

Status indicator and communication monitoring: The variable 'Last Modbus request' always shows when a master last polled. If the Server Socket is deliberately closed ('Active' switched off there, e.g. for a prepared instance not yet in operation), the instance shows 'Inactive' - this is not an error. If the socket is supposed to run but does not reach an active state (e.g. port in use), the instance switches to a real error status instead. With communication monitoring (minutes, 0 = off), the instance additionally reports an error if no Modbus request has arrived for that long - recommended for direct marketing (e.g. 5 min), because 'master no longer polling' is the most important alarm condition there.

Templates: The 'Load template' button fills the register table with a prepared layout (Meteocontrol blue'Log RPC or SunSpec inverter) and sets the matching word order. Nothing is saved until you click 'Apply changes'.

Meteocontrol RPC (direct marketing): The module manages the control registers 5000 (setpoint), 5002-5005 (reserve), 5006 (validity period) and 5008 (watchdog) internally - they do NOT appear in the register table. The template loads the associated actual-value registers (0-14, 100-114, 4000). When the validity period expires, the 'Effective direct marketing setpoint' falls back to the fallback setpoint.

Timeout protection (panel further below): Without the RPC template, the register table has NO expiry date for a written value on its own - a setpoint, once set, stays in place indefinitely if the master loses its connection. For individual writable registers, you can optionally add your own validity period: if the register is not rewritten for that long, the module automatically sets a fallback value - regardless of whether the RPC template is used at all. Example Meteocontrol blue'Log: setpoint register 5000, validity period taken from register 5006 (supplied by the master itself in minutes), fallback value 100 (no curtailment).

The template replaces the contents of the register table in the open configuration and sets the matching word order. The RPC template additionally enables the RPC interface (registers 5000/5006/5008 with watchdog logic) and shows its settings panel. Nothing is saved until you click 'Apply changes'.

Create data points for unassigned registers

For individual writable registers: if the 'Target address' is not written for that long, the module automatically sets the 'Fallback value' - independent of the RPC template, usable for EVERY register table row whose Write setting is not 'No'. 'Duration'+'Unit' apply as fixed values unless a 'Source register' (not 0) is entered - then its CURRENT value supplies the duration (e.g. because the master itself writes a validity period, like register 5006 on Meteocontrol blue'Log). The time only starts running with the FIRST real write access - a row that has never been written never expires automatically, so restarting the instance does not trigger an unwanted fallback. The check runs once per minute; being more precise is not worthwhile for a safety fallback.

Symcon takes over the role of the Meteocontrol blue'Log here itself - NO real blue'Log device is required. Works with any direct marketer that supports the blue'Log RPC interface (e.g. Next Kraftwerke); an existing real blue'Log can continue to run behind it (forwarding via event script).
